title: playmix ai animator
author: missEves
selftext:
i built a tool to create game-ready sprite sheets for any asset w/ ai

* any animated action
* complete character / object consistency
* all art styles
* high quality motion

input a reference image + prompt to animate

export game-ready sprite sheets or animated videos just for fun

[playmix.ai/animate](https://playmix.ai/animate)

replies.author: Careful_Coconut_549

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
website looks clean but:

* you are nudging people too hard to sign up for subscription
* starting people with 0 credit kills your website's own momentum and growth
   * why would anyone pay for a service when they can't even try it out?

Your setup is just encouraging people to pay for another spritesheet generation tool i.e. people can't tell if your tool is better than your competitors but they can end up subscribing to your competitors if they get impatient and run out of credits. Once they are subscribed, they probably won't subscribed another tool for a while...

replies.author: missEves
replies.body:
appreciate your feedback!

it's possible to start a trial which grants free credits you can use immediately. if you aren't happy with it, you can cancel before ever paying for anything.

i'm building this by myself. i used to give away free daily credits without starting a trial and without any nudges (before i launched animation). i reached 37k users and it was costing me thousands of dollars a month. i'm open to iterating, but i can't afford to pay that out of pocket anymore unfortunately.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
you are requiring people to put in their credit card info in order to start a trial. That is not user friendly to say the least. 

I think you should analyze the credit usage data and adjust your credit system accordingly. Or you can experiment with ads. A couple of the ai tools I use are free with ads. 

have you looked at the signup data closely since you gated the signup with the credit card requirement? I can't imagine it working well but that's just me

the tool currently says I have to wait until end of Jan. If I remember, I will check out your tool and see if it solves some of issues I faced with the other spreadsheet gen tools.

Your website looks better than some of your competitors at least. I hope you can make a profit eventually. Good luck

replies.author: missEves
replies.body:
great points! i will definitely adjust the pop-ups. 

i'll also look into options for ads, but my guess is ppl would have to watch a LOT of ads for it to come close to covering the cost. this is not a simple ai chat app. it's a full agent with multimodal text, image, video capabilities, transparency, many ai models including custom tuned ones, heavy backend image and video processing, so it's not cheap.

with the amount of traffic i get, even if i only gave 3 free credits per person i'd still be spending thousands a month on ai for users who mostly will never pay. maybe i will be able to afford to do this in the future when i have a larger base of paying users tho!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I have only been the end user for these ai tools but I have seen some variations with their pricing models:

* some of them don't offer refillable free credits at all but they position themselves as the 'premium option' among their competitors. 
* some have a queuing mechanics to get impatient users to pay for credits
* some have limited features unless the user pays; all their buttons have a free/premium icon so it is pretty clear
* some dont allow commercial use at their free tier 

I honestly dont know if any of them are profitable. Maybe they have investors. I think there are always going to be users who don't pay. Hopefully you can make the numbers work with them in mind. 

I will make a post here when I get around to test the tool. Thanks for the communication and the transparency

comments.author: Shnatrix
comments.body:
Honestly mate - don't listen to the "free = good" crowd....

They aren't the audience you're after.

There should be a way to make this work for everyone though.

I would have a tutorial layer that would give credits enough for one animation.

The tutorial would take the cat you made. You prompt the machine to do something then render.

That process + share + like + twitter etc to get the word out would gain the user 1 animation worth of credits, then go for the nudge.

Yes people just want everything for nothing, but that's not how it works. The alternative is rittle your app with advertising and anyone with an ad blocker must pay to use it.

Have an ads vs no ads or a promote and share for limited access.

They are either advertising for you, or allowing you to advertise to them.

replies.author: missEves
replies.body: i like the tutorial idea! appreciate it

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body:
A nice way for people to earn their credits. Also a good way to tech prompt structuring so they get better outcomes.

I've found as a user - when given the tools with no real guidance. You do the basics 

Walk cycle - wrong direction
Walk cycle left - starts walking left
Continuous walk cycle left loop - perfect

Costs 3x than needed. I think something that teaches users the best way to start.

comments.author: Sasbe93
comments.body: Based on the preview. Shouldn't an animation be created automatically for each generation that returns the sprite to its starting position?

replies.author: missEves

if you check off the seamless loop option yes. otherwise no.

there are use-cases for animations that transition from one state to another, and animations that return to their original state. playmix supports both.

Why not allow the user to make their animations such as standing idle, walking, running, etc which should all be loopable by default. Then show the user a graph of these animations where they can select two, such as standing idle and running, then click "Create Transition" ?

This approach would also be a way to visualize an animation graph before implementation into an engine. Might add extra value to what you're doing.
